name: Cook eggs several different ways
blurb: Scrambled, fried, poached, boiled, coddled and baked — six methods, six sets of heat control lessons, and breakfast is solved forever.
gear: A non-stick pan and a saucepan
steps: Boiled: learn the timings from a rolling boil — 6 minutes for a runny yolk, 8 for jammy, 10 for hard — then straight into ice water.
Fried: learn both sunny-side up over gentle heat with a lid, and crispy-edged over higher heat with hot oil basted over the top.
Scrambled: learn the low-and-slow custardy French style and the fast, large-curd diner style, and taste the difference.
Poached: fresh eggs, barely simmering water with a splash of vinegar, a gentle swirl, three minutes.
Learn to season at the right moment — salt too early in scrambled eggs changes the texture.
Cook each method until it is reliable rather than lucky, and learn what overcooked looks like at each stage.
tips: Egg freshness matters most for poaching; older eggs spread into rags.
Residual heat keeps cooking eggs after they leave the pan. Always pull them slightly underdone.
proof: You cook all six methods to order, correctly, without a timer for the ones that do not need one.
